div.l: And well were esed at the best
And schortely whan̄ the sonne was to rest
So had y spoken̄ with hem eủerychone
That y was of here felawschip̄ anon̄e
And made forward erly to Aryse
To taken oure wey there as y yow devyse
But nathelese while y haue tyme and spase
Or that y further in this tale passe
Me thenketh hit acordant to resoıı̄un
To tellen yow alle the condicyoıı̄un
Of yche of hem as semed me .
And which they were and of which degre
And eke in what aray þey were yn̄
And at a knyght than̄ wol y furst bygyn̄
¶ A knyght þer was and þat a worthy man̄
That fro the tyme that he furst bygan̄
To Ryden̄ oute he loued Chyualery
Treuth honour͗ fredom̄ and curtesye
Full worthy was he in his lordes werr͗e
And þ̉er to had he Ryden̄ dyủerse cuntreys ⁊and ferr͗e
As well in Crystendom̄ as in hethenesse
And eủer honoured for his worthynesse
At Alysaunder he was whan hit was wonne
Full ofte tymes had he þe bord bygonne
Above all nacyoıı̄uns in Pruse ·
In lettewe had he reysed and in Ruse
No crystenman̄ ofter of his degre
In Garnade at the Sege eke had he be
In Algazir͗ and ryden in Belmary
At lyeys was he and at Sataly
